findings.evidence: The new boundary rejects only a Proxy used as fresh.receipt itself, then passes the caller-owned receipt graph directly to readExecutionReceipt. That reader reflects receipt.binding, receipt.process, receipt.outputs, receipt.outputs.stdout/stderr, and receipt.result. A plain top-level receipt containing a Proxy at any of those nested paths can therefore execute getPrototypeOf or ownKeys traps before the candidate converts the thrown error to FRESH_RECEIPT_INVALID. The current zero-trap regression covers hostile fresh.expected and nativeReport/outcomes, but not these nested receipt paths.
findings.requiredFix: Before readExecutionReceipt, recursively validate and snapshot the exact receipt schema with Proxy-first checks at the top receipt and every nested record/list boundary, without reading caller properties or invoking getters; pass that data-only snapshot and the original issued expectation to readExecutionReceipt. Add deterministic counters for Proxy and revoked-Proxy values at binding, process, outputs, stdout, stderr, and result. Each must return FRESH_RECEIPT_INVALID with zero traps. Keep handle consumption fail-closed and do not add a shape-only receipt acceptance path.
